items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: 2024 in Review
notes: Cari Van Niekerk, Director, Corporate Communications gave a presentation with highlights from staff across the City.

items.title: Short Term Rental Licensing By-law Update
notes: Grant Curlew gave a presentation detailing the background of potential Short-Term Rental regulations at the City, the results of the engagement completed, and the proposed regulations. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Draft Plan of Subdivision 30T-24401,
notes: 651-663 Erb St W, and Lands Owned by
(Southwest Corner of Erb St W and
Wendy Fisher gave a presentation outlining the proposal, including background of the site and the proposed Zoning By-law and Official Plan Amendments. She then responded to questions of Council.
Dave Aston, Partner, MHBC Planning gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development. He then responded to questions of Council.

Scott Patterson, Principal, Patterson Planning Consultants Inc. on behalf of Kieswetter Development Corp., owner of 41 Ira Needles Blvd, spoke about the impact of the stormwater management system on the neighbouring properties and the proposed road alignment. Wendy Fisher responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

motions.text: That Council hold a closed meeting for the purposes of considering the following subject matter: a) personal matters about an identifiable individual, including municipal or local board employees (human resource update, committee appointments); and, b) labour relations or employee negotiations (human resource update); and, c) a proposed or pending acquisition or disposition of land by the municipality or local board (potential disposition of city owned lands); and, d) advice that is subject to solicitor-client privilege, including communications necessary for that purpose (potential disposition of city owned-lands); and, e) litigation or potential litigation, including matters before administrative tribunals, affecting the municipality or local board (potential disposition of city owned-lands).

motions.item_title: Short Term Rental Licensing By-law Update
motions.text: 1. That Council approve report COM2025-004. 2. That Council approve the amending by-law to the Residential Rental Licensing By-law #2011-047. 3. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Federal Government’s Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund. 4. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation and return to Council with recommendations on a comprehensive update to the rental licensing by-law, including low- rise, short-term, and mid/high-rise rental regulations by the conclusion of the Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund program on March 31, 2027.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report COM2025-004.

2. That Council approve the amending by-law to the Residential Rental Licensing By-law #2011-047.

3. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant submission to the Federal Government’s Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund.

4. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation and return to Council with recommendations on a comprehensive update to the rental licensing by-law, including low- rise, short-term, and mid/high-rise rental regulations by the conclusion of the Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund program on March 31, 2027.

motions.item_title: Mayor McCabe - AMO’s “Municipalities Under Pressure” Motion (2025)
motions.text: Motion to be tabled January 20, 2025 for Council consideration January 27, 2025. Motion: WHEREAS the Association of Municipalities of Ontario in partnership the Ontario Municipal Social Services Association (OMSSA) and the Northern Ontario Service Deliverers Association (NOSDA) collaborated with HelpSeeker Technologies to research and release a comprehensive study that reveals the massive growth of homelessness in Ontario, and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo is a member municipality of the Association of Ontario Municipalities and works in partnership with them including having the Mayor as a member of AMO’s Board of Directors, and WHEREAS this comprehensive report supports OBCM’s ongoing Solve The Crisis campaign and its key requests of the provincial and the federal government to address the homelessness crisis, NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that: 1) The City of Waterloo endorse the “Municipalities Under Pressure – the Human and Financial Cost of Ontario’s Homelessness Crisis” report and work in collaboration with AMO to advance the key findings and recommendations of this report and OBCM’s Solve the Crisis Campaign. 2) And that a copy of this motion be sent to: • The Hon, Justin Trudeau, Prime Minister of Canada • The Hon. Nathaniel Erskine-Smith, Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities • The Hon. Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario • The Hon. Paul Calandra, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing • The Hon. Vijay Thanigasalam, Associate Minister of Housing • MPP Matthew Rae, Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing • Local area MPPs and MPs • Robin Jones, President, AMO and Mayor of Westport • Karen Redman, Chair, MARCO and Chair of the Region of Waterloo • Neighbouring municipalities • The Association of Municipalities of Ontario • The Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus
